source.text: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν παρ’ ὑμῖν μένων·

records.literal_gloss: These things I have spoken to you beside you remaining.

en.L: These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you.
en.B: I have told you these things while I am still with you.
en.R: I have told you these things while I am still here with you.

es.L: Estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} he hablado mientras permanezco con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dicho estas cosas mientras todavía estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dicho estas cosas mientras todavía estoy aquí con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Ces choses, je vous les ai dites en demeurant auprès de vous.
fr.B: Je vous ai dit cela pendant que je suis encore avec vous.
fr.R: Je vous ai dit ces choses pendant que je suis encore ici avec vous.

sw.L: Mambo haya nimewaambia nikikaa pamoja nanyi.
sw.B: Nimewaambia mambo haya wakati bado niko pamoja nanyi.
sw.R: Nimewaambia mambo haya wakati bado niko hapa pamoja nanyi.

vi.L: Những điều này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn ở với các con.
vi.B: Ta đã nói với các con những điều này trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn ở với các con.
vi.R: Ta đã nói với các con những điều này trong lúc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn ở đây với các con.

ko.L: 너희 곁에 머물러 있는 동안 내가 이것들을 너희에게 말하였다.
ko.B: 내가 아직 너희와 함께 있는 동안에 이것들을 너희에게 말했다.
ko.R: 나는 아직 여기 너희와 함께 있는 동안에 이것들을 너희에게 말해 주었다.

pt.L: Estas coisas eu lhes falei enquanto permaneço com vocês.
pt.B: Eu lhes disse estas coisas enquanto ainda estou com vocês.
pt.R: Eu disse estas coisas a vocês enquanto ainda estou aqui com vocês.

decisions.choice: remaining with you: staying in their company, still present with them
alternatives: remaining in the theological sense of a lasting union (15:4-10)
decisions.reason: Here the verb has its ordinary sense: Jesus is still with them, but not for long (13:33; 14:28). The same words, "remains with you", were just used of the Spirit (14:17). The Spirit will stay with the disciples as Jesus is about to stop doing in the same way, which leads into verse 26.

decisions.choice: these things I have spoken: the teaching he has given them up to now, especially this evening
decisions.reason: "These things" looks back over what he has said (also 15:11; 16:1, 4, 25, 33). It sets what Jesus has said while present against what the Spirit will teach and bring back to their minds after he has gone (verse 26).

decisions.choice: while I am still with you (B); still here with you (R)
decisions.reason: "Still" brings out what the participle implies in this setting: his time with them is coming to an end (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "remaining" so the link with 14:17 can be seen.

decisions.choice: mientras todavía estoy (aquí) con ustedes
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "permanecer".

decisions.choice: speech tenses: passé composé for the Greek perfects and aorists ("je vous ai dit"), present and future as in the Greek, at every level
alternatives: passé simple for the past tenses of speech ("je vous dis")
decisions.reason: This passage (14:25-31) is all Jesus's speech, so it has no narrative tense to settle; inside speech every level uses the passé composé, as people speak and as the rest of John's French does (see 1:19). It serves both for the Greek perfect ("I have spoken", verse 25) and for the aorist ("I said", verse 26). Literal keeps "en demeurant auprès de vous", which echoes "il demeure auprès de vous" said of the Spirit in 14:17 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Ta ... các con (Jesus to the disciples)
decisions.reason: As set for the whole book: Jesus says "Ta" of himself (the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence) and "các con" to his disciples. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체) and gives the Father and the Spirit the honorific ("께서", -시-, "그분")
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Recorded once for 14:25-31.

decisions.choice: permaneço (L); estou (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "permanecer", the verb used of the Spirit in 14:17 ("permanece com vocês"), so that the link the English Literal keeps can be seen. Balanced and Readable use the plain "estar", since here the verb has its ordinary sense (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ὁ δὲ παράκλητος, τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ὃ πέμψει ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐκεῖνος ὑμᾶς διδάξει πάντα καὶ ὑπομνήσει ὑμᾶς πάντα ἃ εἶπον ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: The but advocate, the Spirit the Holy, which will send the Father in the name of me, that one you will teach all things and will remind you all things which I said to you.

en.L: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will teach you all things and will remind you of all things that I said to you.
en.B: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father is going to send in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, is the one who will teach you everything and remind you of all I have said to you.
en.R: But the Father will send the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. He will teach you everything. He will remind you of everything I have told you.

es.L: Pero el Defensor, el Espíritu Santo, a quien el Padre enviará en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñará todas las cosas y {{plural_you:les|os}} recordará todo lo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho.
es.B: Pero el Defensor, el Espíritu Santo, a quien el Padre va a enviar en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, es quien {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñará todas las cosas y {{plural_you:les|os}} recordará todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho.
es.R: Pero el Padre enviará en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre al Defensor, el Espíritu Santo. Él {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñará todas las cosas. Él {{plural_you:les|os}} recordará todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho.

fr.L: Mais le Défenseur, l’Esprit Saint, que le Père enverra en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous enseignera toutes choses et vous rappellera tout ce que je vous ai dit.
fr.B: Mais le Défenseur, l’Esprit Saint, que le Père va envoyer en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui vous enseignera tout et qui vous fera souvenir de tout ce que je vous ai dit.
fr.R: Mais le Père enverra le Défenseur, l’Esprit Saint, en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Il vous enseignera tout. Il vous rappellera tout ce que je vous ai dit.

sw.L: Lakini yule Mtetezi, Roho Mtakatifu, ambaye Baba atamtuma kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, huyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawafundisha kila kitu na kuwakumbusha kila kitu nilichowaambia.
sw.B: Lakini Mtetezi, Roho Mtakatifu, ambaye Baba atamtuma kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ndiye atakayewafundisha kila kitu na kuwakumbusha yote niliyowaambia.
sw.R: Lakini Baba atamtuma Mtetezi, Roho Mtakatifu, kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Yeye atawafundisha kila kitu. Atawakumbusha kila kitu nilichowaambia.

vi.L: Nhưng Đấng Biện Hộ, là Đức Thánh Linh, Đấng mà Cha sẽ sai đến trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ dạy các con mọi điều và sẽ nhắc các con nhớ mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con.
vi.B: Nhưng Đấng Biện Hộ, là Đức Thánh Linh, Đấng mà Cha sẽ sai đến nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ dạy dỗ các con mọi điều và nhắc các con nhớ lại tất cả những gì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con.
vi.R: Nhưng Cha sẽ nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sai Đấng Biện Hộ, là Đức Thánh Linh, đến. Ngài sẽ dạy các con mọi điều. Ngài sẽ nhắc các con nhớ lại mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con.

ko.L: 그러나 변호자, 곧 아버지께서 내 이름으로 보내실 성령, 그분께서 너희에게 모든 것을 가르치시고, 내가 너희에게 말한 모든 것을 생각나게 하실 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 아버지께서 내 이름으로 보내실 변호자, 곧 성령께서 너희에게 모든 것을 가르쳐 주시고, 내가 너희에게 한 말을 모두 생각나게 해 주실 것이다.
ko.R: 아버지께서 내 이름으로 변호자, 곧 성령을 보내실 것이다. 그분께서 너희에게 모든 것을 가르쳐 주실 것이다. 또 내가 너희에게 한 말을 모두 다시 생각나게 해 주실 것이다.

pt.L: Mas o Defensor, o Espírito Santo, a quem o Pai enviará em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes ensinará todas as coisas e lhes fará lembrar todas as coisas que eu lhes disse.
pt.B: Mas o Defensor, o Espírito Santo, que o Pai vai enviar em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome, é quem lhes ensinará tudo e os fará lembrar de tudo o que eu lhes disse.
pt.R: Mas o Pai vai enviar o Defensor, o Espírito Santo, em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome. Ele vai ensinar tudo a vocês. Ele vai fazer vocês lembrarem de tudo o que eu disse a vocês.

decisions.choice: the Advocate: one called to stand beside another and speak or act for them
decisions.reason: The word was used of someone who stands by a person, above all in a court, to plead for them. In John the setting is testimony and judgment: the Advocate testifies about Jesus (15:26) and proves the world wrong (16:8-11). He also teaches and reminds (here) and guides (16:13), so the help he gives is wider than the courtroom. 1 John 2:1 uses the same word of Jesus pleading with the Father; 14:16 calls the Spirit "another" Advocate, so Jesus has been one for them already.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit: God's own Spirit, the Advocate promised in 14:16-17
decisions.reason: "The Holy Spirit" names the Advocate and shows who he is: the Spirit of God, called "the Spirit of truth" in 14:17. It is the Spirit who came down on Jesus (1:32-33) and whom he will give to those who believe in him (7:39; 20:22).

decisions.choice: a neuter relative pronoun, then a masculine one: grammatical agreement, with the Advocate spoken of as a person
alternatives: the neuter means the Spirit is an impersonal force
the masculine is a deliberate statement that the Spirit is a person
decisions.reason: The word for spirit is neuter, so the pronoun that follows it ("which") is neuter by the rules of Greek grammar, as in 14:17; this says nothing about whether the Spirit is a thing. The resuming word "that one" is masculine, agreeing with "the Advocate" at the head of the sentence, so grammar can explain it too, and it does not prove a point on its own. What shows the Spirit as personal is what he does: he is sent, teaches, reminds, testifies (15:26), hears and speaks (16:13). The masculine word is emphatic: he and no other will teach them.

decisions.choice: in my name: sent on Jesus's behalf, as his representative and in answer to his request
alternatives: sent to make Jesus's name known
decisions.reason: To act in someone's name is to act with their authority and on their behalf (5:43; 10:25). Jesus has said he will ask the Father to send the Advocate (14:16); the Father sends him as Jesus's representative, to carry on what Jesus has begun.

decisions.choice: teach all things and remind of all that Jesus said: two sides of one work, centered on Jesus's own words
alternatives: all things: every kind of knowledge
decisions.reason: "All things" is defined by the second clause: the Spirit's teaching brings back to mind and opens up what Jesus said. John shows this happening: after Jesus was raised, the disciples remembered what he had said and understood it (2:22; 12:16). The Spirit does not bring a different message but makes Jesus's message known (16:13-14).

decisions.choice: the Advocate
decisions.reason: The book uses "the Advocate" at every level, because John's setting is testimony and judgment (meaning decision m1). Other well-known renderings are Helper, Counselor and Comforter; each catches part of the sense.

decisions.choice: whom; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The Spirit is never "it" in this translation. The neuter Greek pronoun is grammatical agreement only (meaning decision m3), so English uses the personal "who", "whom" and "he". "He" takes the deity pronoun setting like every pronoun for God; the relatives "who" and "whom" do not, as nowhere else in the translation does a relative pronoun take it. Balanced turns "he" into "is the one who" to keep the emphasis of the masculine word; Readable starts new sentences with plain "He".

decisions.choice: Defensor
decisions.reason: As in 14:16.

decisions.choice: a quien; él for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" for the Spirit takes the setting; at the start of a Readable sentence it is written plain.

decisions.choice: le Défenseur
decisions.reason: The book-wide French word for this title, as in 14:16 (meaning decision m1), where the choice and the other renderings are explained.

decisions.choice: que ...; {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} (L); c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui (B)
decisions.reason: The neuter relative is grammatical agreement only (meaning decision m3); French "que" has no gender. The masculine "that one" stresses the Advocate as the one who will teach; Literal gives the stress with "lui, il" and Balanced with "c’est lui qui", both pronouns for the Spirit with the deity_pronoun setting. Readable starts new sentences with a plain "Il".

decisions.choice: Đấng Biện Hộ; "Đấng mà" and "Ngài" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for parakletos, as in 14:16; the footnote gives "Đấng Yên Ủi" (Comforter) and "Đấng Trợ Giúp" (Helper). The Spirit is spoken of as a person ("Đấng mà", "Ngài"), whatever the gender of the Greek pronouns.

decisions.choice: "변호자" at every level, as in 14:16; "그분께서" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for the paraklētos (style guide, section 6). The Spirit is spoken of as a person with the honorific, whatever the gender of the Greek pronouns (meaning decision).

source.text: εἰρήνην ἀφίημι ὑμῖν, εἰρήνην τὴν ἐμὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν· οὐ καθὼς ὁ κόσμος δίδωσιν ἐγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Peace I leave to you, peace the my I give to you; not as the world gives I give to you.

en.L: Peace I leave with you; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you.
en.B: Peace I leave with you; it is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own peace that I give you. I do not give the way the world gives.
en.R: I am leaving you peace. I am giving you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own peace. I do not give the way the world gives.

es.L: La paz {{plural_you:les|os}} dejo; {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} paz {{plural_you:les|os}} doy. No como el mundo [la] da, {{plural_you:se la|os la}} doy yo.
es.B: La paz {{plural_you:les|os}} dejo; es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia paz la que {{plural_you:les|os}} doy. Yo no {{plural_you:se la|os la}} doy como la da el mundo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} dejo la paz. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} doy {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia paz. Yo no la doy como la da el mundo.

fr.L: La paix, je vous la laisse ; {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} paix, je vous la donne. Ce n’est pas comme le monde donne que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous donne.
fr.B: La paix, je vous la laisse ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre paix que je vous donne. Je ne donne pas à la manière du monde.
fr.R: En partant, je vous laisse la paix. Je vous donne {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre paix. Ce que je donne n’est pas comme ce que donne le monde.

sw.L: Amani ninawaachia; amani iliyo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ninawapa. Si kama ulimwengu unavyotoa ninavyowapa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Amani ninawaachia; ni amani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ninayowapa. Sitoi kama ulimwengu unavyotoa.
sw.R: Ninawaachia amani. Ninawapa amani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Sitoi kama ulimwengu unavyotoa.

vi.L: Bình an {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} để lại cho các con; bình an của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho các con. Không như thế gian ban, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho các con.
vi.B: Ta để lại bình an cho các con; chính bình an của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho các con. Ta không ban cho các con như cách thế gian ban.
vi.R: Ta để lại cho các con sự bình an. Ta ban cho các con chính sự bình an của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta không ban như cách thế gian ban.

ko.L: 평안을 너희에게 남겨 둔다. 나의 평안을 너희에게 준다. 세상이 주는 것과 같이 내가 너희에게 주는 것이 아니다.
ko.B: 나는 너희에게 평안을 남겨 준다. 내가 너희에게 주는 것은 바로 나의 평안이다. 나는 세상이 주는 방식으로 주지 않는다.
ko.R: 나는 너희에게 평안을 남겨 주고 간다. 내 평안을 너희에게 준다. 내가 주는 평안은 세상이 주는 것과 다르다.

pt.L: Paz eu deixo a vocês; a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} paz eu lhes dou. Não como o mundo dá eu lhes dou.
pt.B: A paz eu deixo com vocês; é a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} própria paz que eu lhes dou. Eu não dou como o mundo dá.
pt.R: Eu estou deixando a paz para vocês. Eu estou dando a vocês a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} própria paz. Eu não dou como o mundo dá.

decisions.choice: peace: the farewell wish of shalom, given new content as Jesus's own gift
alternatives: peace as the absence of war or conflict
decisions.reason: "Peace" was the ordinary greeting and farewell among Jews, a wish for wholeness and well-being from God. Jesus, about to leave, uses the parting word but does more than wish it: he leaves it and gives it, and it is "my" peace. It is the peace he has with the Father and gives to those who are his, the peace they may have "in me" even in the world's trouble (16:33). The risen Jesus greets them with the same word (20:19, 21, 26). Peace is a key term.

decisions.choice: leave: leave behind as a parting gift, as someone going away leaves something to those who stay
decisions.reason: The verb often means to let go or forgive, but here, with "to you", it means to leave something behind for others. The words are those of one who is departing (14:28).

decisions.choice: not as the world gives: unlike the world's peace, Jesus's gift is real and does not depend on circumstances
alternatives: not in the way the world gives presents
decisions.reason: The contrast is with the world in John's sense, human life apart from God. The world can wish peace, as in a greeting, or offer a peace that lasts only while things go well; it has trouble to give (16:33). Jesus gives what he says, and his peace holds when he is put to death and they are scattered (16:32-33). The "I" is emphatic, setting his giving against the world's.

decisions.choice: Peace I leave with you
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "peace" first in both clauses, and there is no natural way to keep that order other than the familiar wording. Balanced keeps it for the first clause and then stresses "my own peace". Readable uses ordinary word order.

decisions.choice: my own peace
decisions.reason: The Greek has a fuller form of "my", standing after the noun with its own article, which stresses it. "Own" carries that stress.

decisions.choice: La paz les dejo
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "peace" first, as a farewell (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: La paix, je vous la laisse ; ma paix, je vous la donne (L); La paix, je vous la laisse (B)
alternatives: Je vous laisse la paix, je vous donne ma paix
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "peace" first in both clauses. Unlike English, French can keep that order naturally by placing the noun first and picking it up with "la", so Literal does so twice and Balanced once. Literal also keeps the stressed "I" of the last clause with "moi, je" (a pronoun for Christ, with the setting). Readable adds "En partant" to say that this is a parting gift (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: bình an
decisions.reason: "Bình an" is the book-wide key term for peace, the farewell wish given new content as Jesus's gift. Literal keeps the Greek order with "bình an" first.

decisions.choice: "평안" at every level
decisions.reason: The Korean key term for eirēnē in John (style guide, section 6). "평안" is inner peace and well-being, close to the farewell wish of shalom that the meaning decision describes; "평화" leans toward the absence of war, and "평강" is now mainly church language.

source.text: μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία μηδὲ δειλιάτω.

records.literal_gloss: Not let be troubled of you the heart nor let it be fearful.

en.L: Do not let your heart be troubled, nor let it be fearful.
en.B: Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them give way to fear.
en.R: Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not be afraid.

es.L: No se turbe {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, ni tenga miedo.
es.B: Que no se angustie {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, ni se deje vencer por el miedo.
es.R: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nada {{plural_you:los|os}} angustie, y no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo.

fr.L: Que votre cœur ne soit pas troublé, et qu’il ne soit pas craintif.
fr.B: Ne laissez pas le trouble envahir vos cœurs, et ne vous laissez pas gagner par la peur.
fr.R: Ne soyez pas bouleversés, et n’ayez pas peur.

sw.L: Moyo wenu usifadhaike, wala usiwe na woga.
sw.B: Mioyo yenu isifadhaike, wala isikubali kushindwa na hofu.

vi.L: Lòng các con đừng bối rối, cũng đừng sợ hãi.
vi.B: Các con đừng để lòng mình bối rối, cũng đừng để lòng mình khiếp sợ.
vi.R: Các con đừng lo lắng, cũng đừng sợ hãi.

ko.L: 너희 마음이 흔들리지 않게 하고, 겁내지도 않게 하여라.
ko.B: 너희는 마음이 흔들리지 않게 하고, 두려움에 꺾이지 않게 하여라.

pt.L: Não se perturbe o coração de vocês, nem se acovarde.
pt.B: Não deixem que o coração de vocês se perturbe, e não cedam ao medo.
pt.R: Não fiquem com o coração aflito, e não tenham medo.

alignments.target_span: let them give way to fear

decisions.choice: the same command as 14:1, closing the first part of the farewell talk
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the words he began with in 14:1. The repeat frames what lies between: his going to the Father, his coming back, the Spirit and the peace he leaves give them reason not to be troubled. The word for "troubled" was used of Jesus himself as he faced death (11:33; 12:27; 13:21).

decisions.choice: your heart: one heart for many people, each one's heart
alternatives: the group as a whole, with one shared heart
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural but "heart" is singular, as in 14:1. Greek often speaks so of something each person has one of. The sense is each of them, inwardly.

decisions.choice: be fearful: lose courage, shrink back in fear before danger
alternatives: be cowardly in a shameful sense
decisions.reason: The verb, found only here in the New Testament, means to be timid or lose heart when danger comes. The related noun and adjective are used for cowardice and fearfulness (Matthew 8:26; 2 Timothy 1:7). Jesus is not scolding them; he tells them not to let fear master them as the hour comes (14:30).

decisions.choice: your hearts (B, R); give way to fear (B); do not be afraid (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make "hearts" plural, the natural way to speak of many people's hearts (meaning decision m2). This sentence should read the same as 14:1. Balanced says "give way to fear" for the sense of losing courage; Readable says it simply.

decisions.choice: the wording of 14:1
decisions.reason: The same command as 14:1 (meaning decision m1), in the same Spanish words at each level.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 14:1 at each level
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the words he began with in 14:1 (meaning decision m1), so each level repeats its French from there. Balanced "ne vous laissez pas gagner par la peur" gives the sense of losing courage before danger (m3); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "마음이 흔들리지 않게 하여라" (L, B), as in 14:1
decisions.reason: The same command as 14:1 (meaning decision), so Korean repeats the same wording and the reader hears the echo.

decisions.choice: o coração de vocês (L, B); com o coração aflito (R)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable make "hearts" plural. Portuguese speaks of what each person has one of in the singular ("o coração de vocês"), as the Greek does (meaning decision m2), so the singular reads naturally at every level.

source.text: ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν· Ὑπάγω καὶ ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: You heard that I said to you, "I go away and I come to you."

en.L: You heard that I said to you, 'I am going away, and I am coming to you.'
en.B: You heard {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tell you, 'I am leaving, and I am coming back to you.'
en.R: You heard {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tell you, 'I am going away, but I will come back to you.'

es.B: Me {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} decir{{plural_you:les|os}}: “Me voy, y vuelvo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.
es.R: Me {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} decir{{plural_you:les|os}}: “Me voy, pero volveré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}”.

fr.B: Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez entendu vous dire : “Je pars, et je reviens vers vous.”
fr.R: Vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez entendu vous dire : “Je m’en vais, mais je reviendrai vers vous.”

vi.B: Các con đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo các con: 'Ta ra đi, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại với các con.'
vi.R: Các con đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói: 'Ta sẽ đi xa, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trở lại với các con.'

ko.L: 너희는 내가 너희에게 '나는 간다. 그리고 너희에게 온다' 하고 말한 것을 들었다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 '나는 떠나간다. 그리고 너희에게 돌아온다'라고 한 말을 너희는 들었다.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 '나는 떠나지만 너희에게 다시 돌아올 것이다'라고 한 말을 너희는 들었다.

pt.L: Vocês ouviram que eu lhes disse: 'Vou embora e venho até vocês.'
pt.B: Vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouviram dizer: 'Vou partir e voltarei para vocês.'
pt.R: Vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouviram dizer: 'Eu vou embora, mas vou voltar para vocês.'

decisions.choice: I am going away and I am coming: present tenses that look to what is about to happen
decisions.reason: Jesus refers back to what he has said in this talk (14:2-4, 18). Both verbs are present, as is common in Greek of something certain and near: the going has already begun, and the coming is as sure.

decisions.choice: I am coming to you: his return to them after his death, which may include his coming at the end
alternatives: only his coming at the end of the age
only his coming in the Spirit
decisions.reason: In 14:18-19 the coming is soon ("in a little while ... you will see me"), which fits his appearing after the resurrection (20:19-20) and his presence through the Spirit (14:23). In 14:3 he speaks of coming again to take them to himself. The text does not separate these, and the words here can include them all.

decisions.choice: leaving, and I am coming back (B); I will come back (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "leaving" for the plain going away. "Back" makes clear that the one who goes is the one who comes. Readable uses the future for the present tense that points ahead (meaning decision m1) and "but" to show the contrast.

decisions.choice: vuelvo (B); volveré (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

source.text: εἰ ἠγαπᾶτέ με ἐχάρητε ἄν, ὅτι πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα, ὅτι ὁ πατὴρ μείζων μού ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: If you were loving me, you would have rejoiced, that I go to the Father, because the Father greater than me is.

en.L: If you loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
en.B: If you loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you would be glad I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I am.
en.R: If you loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you would be glad that I am going to the Father, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is greater than I am.

es.L: Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:amaran|amarais}}, {{plural_you:se habrían alegrado|os habríais alegrado}} de que voy al Padre, porque el Padre es mayor que yo.
es.B: Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:amaran|amarais}}, {{plural_you:se alegrarían|os alegraríais}} de que voy al Padre, porque el Padre es mayor que yo.
es.R: Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:amaran|amarais}}, {{plural_you:se alegrarían|os alegraríais}} de que voy al Padre, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es mayor que yo.

fr.L: Si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimiez, vous vous seriez réjouis de ce que je vais vers le Père, parce que le Père est plus grand que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimiez, vous seriez heureux que j’aille vers le Père, car le Père est plus grand que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimiez, vous seriez contents que j’aille vers le Père, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est plus grand que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Kama mngelinipenda, mngefurahi kwamba ninakwenda kwa Baba, kwa maana Baba ni mkubwa kuliko {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Kama mngenipenda, mngefurahi kwamba ninakwenda kwa Baba, kwa kuwa Baba ni mkuu kuliko {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.R: Kama mngenipenda, mngefurahi kwamba ninakwenda kwa Baba, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mkuu kuliko {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

vi.L: Nếu các con yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì các con hẳn đã vui mừng vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về cùng Cha, vì Cha lớn hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Nếu các con yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, các con hẳn sẽ vui mừng vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về với Cha, vì Cha lớn hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Nếu các con yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, các con sẽ vui vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về với Cha, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lớn hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 너희가 나를 사랑하였다면, 내가 아버지께로 가는 것을 기뻐하였을 것이다. 아버지께서 나보다 크시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 너희가 나를 사랑했다면 내가 아버지께로 가는 것을 기뻐했을 것이다. 아버지께서는 나보다 크신 분이기 때문이다.
ko.R: 너희가 나를 정말 사랑한다면 내가 아버지께로 가는 것을 기뻐할 텐데. 아버지께서는 나보다 크신 분이다.

pt.L: Se vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} amassem, teriam se alegrado de que eu vou para o Pai, porque o Pai é maior do que eu.
pt.B: Se vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} amassem, ficariam contentes por eu ir para o Pai, pois o Pai é maior do que eu.
pt.R: Se vocês {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} amassem, ficariam felizes de eu estar indo para o Pai, pois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é maior do que eu.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: their love is not yet glad for him
alternatives: a flat denial that they love him at all
decisions.reason: The form says the condition is not met: if you loved me (as love would), you would have rejoiced. Jesus does not deny that they love him (14:21, 23; 16:27). Their grief looks at their own loss; love that looked at him would be glad that he goes home to the Father.

decisions.choice: the Father is greater: as the one who sent the Son, to whom the Son, having done what he was sent to do, now returns
alternatives: greater than the Son in the humble state he took on earth
decisions.reason: The sentence gives the reason for gladness: Jesus is going to the one who sent him (7:33; 16:5) and will share again the glory he had with him (17:5). Throughout John the Father is the one who sends and commands and the Son the one sent, who does his will (5:19, 30; 8:29; 14:31). The same Gospel says that the Word was God (1:1) and records Jesus saying "I and the Father are one" (10:30), and his claims were heard as making himself equal to God (5:18). This sentence speaks of the Son's relation to the Father in his mission; it does not discuss what the Father and the Son are in their being. The word "greater" has been understood in more than one way.

decisions.choice: because I am going to the Father (SBLGNT)
alternatives: because I said, I am going to the Father (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "I said" before "I am going", repeating the words of the first half of the verse. The earliest manuscripts lack it. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Father (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "my Father is greater than I". The earliest manuscripts have "the Father". The sense is not changed. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: would be glad
decisions.reason: In English the past form "would have rejoiced" can sound as if the moment were over; the gladness Jesus means belongs to now, as he goes. "Glad" is the everyday word.

decisions.choice: se alegrarían
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1); the reflexive sits inside the ustedes / vosotros span.

decisions.choice: plus grand que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}
alternatives: plus grand que je ne suis
decisions.reason: French compares with the stressed pronoun ("que moi"), where English says "than I"; as a pronoun for Christ it takes the deity_pronoun setting. Literal keeps the past conditional "vous vous seriez réjouis"; Balanced and Readable use the present conditional, as the English uses "would be glad".

decisions.choice: hẳn đã vui mừng (L); hẳn sẽ vui mừng (B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks a condition contrary to fact with "hẳn" (surely would), as in 14:7.

source.text: καὶ νῦν εἴρηκα ὑμῖν πρὶν γενέσθαι, ἵνα ὅταν γένηται πιστεύσητε.

records.literal_gloss: And now I have told you before to happen, so that whenever it happens you may believe.

en.L: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
en.B: I have told you now, before it takes place, so that when it does take place you will believe.
en.R: I have told you this now, before it happens. Then, when it happens, you will believe.

es.L: Y ahora {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} he dicho antes de que suceda, para que, cuando suceda, {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Se lo|Os lo}} he dicho ahora, antes de que suceda, para que, cuando suceda, {{plural_you:crean|creáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dicho esto ahora, antes de que suceda. Así, cuando suceda, {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}}.

fr.L: Et maintenant je vous [l’]ai dit avant que cela n’arrive, afin que, lorsque cela arrivera, vous croyiez.
fr.B: Je vous l’ai dit dès maintenant, avant que cela arrive, pour que, quand cela arrivera, vous croyiez.
fr.R: Je vous ai dit cela maintenant, avant que cela arrive. Ainsi, quand cela arrivera, vous croirez.

sw.L: Na sasa nimekwisha kuwaambia kabla halijatokea, ili litakapotokea mwamini.
sw.B: Nimewaambia sasa, kabla halijatukia, ili litakapotukia mwamini.
sw.R: Nimewaambia jambo hili sasa, kabla halijatokea. Kisha, litakapotokea, mtaamini.

vi.L: Và bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con trước khi việc ấy xảy ra, để khi việc ấy xảy ra, các con tin.
vi.B: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói trước với các con, trước khi việc ấy xảy ra, để khi việc ấy xảy đến, các con sẽ tin.
vi.R: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói điều này với các con trước khi nó xảy ra. Rồi khi nó xảy ra, các con sẽ tin.

ko.L: 그리고 이제 그 일이 일어나기 전에 내가 너희에게 말하였다. 그 일이 일어날 때에 너희가 믿게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 이 일이 일어나기 전에 내가 지금 너희에게 말해 두었다. 그것이 일어날 때에 너희가 믿게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 이 일이 일어나기 전에 지금 너희에게 말해 주었다. 그러면 그 일이 일어날 때 너희가 믿을 것이다.

pt.L: E agora eu lhes disse antes de acontecer, para que, quando acontecer, vocês creiam.
pt.B: Eu lhes disse isso agora, antes que aconteça, para que, quando acontecer, vocês creiam.
pt.R: Eu estou contando isso a vocês agora, antes que aconteça. Assim, quando acontecer, vocês vão acreditar.

decisions.choice: the same purpose as in 13:19: what Jesus foretells will, when it comes true, lead them to believe
decisions.reason: In 13:19 Jesus said the same about Judas's betrayal, adding "that I am". Here "believe" stands without an object: they will believe in him, seeing that what he said came true (2:22). Foretelling what is to come marks the true God in Isaiah (Isaiah 41:22-23; 46:9-10).

decisions.choice: it happens: his going away to the Father through his death, and his coming again
decisions.reason: The unnamed "it" is what he has just spoken of in verse 28: his departure to the Father, which takes place through his arrest and death, and his return to them.

decisions.choice: this
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "this" for what Jesus has told them, which the Greek leaves understood, and splits the sentence.

decisions.choice: the wording of 13:19
decisions.reason: The same purpose as 13:19 (meaning decision m1), in the same Spanish words.

source.text: οὐκέτι πολλὰ λαλήσω μεθ’ ὑμῶν, ἔρχεται γὰρ ὁ τοῦ κόσμου ἄρχων· καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ οὐκ ἔχει οὐδέν, ἀλλ’ ἵνα γνῷ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι ἀγαπῶ τὸν πατέρα, καὶ καθὼς ἐνετείλατο μοι ὁ πατὴρ οὕτως ποιῶ.

records.literal_gloss: No longer many things I will speak with you, comes for the of the world ruler; and in me he has not nothing, \v 31 but so that may know the world that I love the Father, and as commanded me the Father, so I do.

en.L: I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} he has nothing; \v 31 but so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father commanded {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I do.
en.B: I will not say much more to you, for the ruler of the world is coming. He has no hold on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 31 But so that the world will know that I love the Father, I do exactly as the Father has commanded {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I will not talk with you much longer, because Satan, the ruler of the world, is coming. He has no power over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 31 But I do just what the Father has told {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do, so that the world will know that I love the Father.

es.L: Ya no hablaré mucho con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque viene el gobernante del mundo, y en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no tiene nada; \v 31 pero para que el mundo sepa que amo al Padre, y como el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mandó, así hago.
es.B: Ya no hablaré mucho más con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque viene el gobernante del mundo. Él no tiene ningún poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \v 31 Pero, para que el mundo sepa que amo al Padre, hago exactamente lo que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha mandado.
es.R: Ya no voy a hablar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mucho más, porque viene Satanás, el que gobierna el mundo. No tiene ningún poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \v 31 Pero yo hago exactamente lo que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha mandado, para que el mundo sepa que amo al Padre.

fr.L: Je ne parlerai plus beaucoup avec vous, car le prince du monde vient ; et en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} il n’a rien ; \v 31 mais afin que le monde sache que j’aime le Père, et comme le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a commandé, ainsi je fais.
fr.B: Je ne vous parlerai plus beaucoup, car le prince du monde vient. Il n’a aucune prise sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \v 31 Mais pour que le monde sache que j’aime le Père, je fais exactement ce que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a commandé.
fr.R: Je ne vais plus parler longtemps avec vous, parce que Satan, celui qui domine le monde, arrive. Il n’a aucun pouvoir sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \v 31 Mais je fais exactement ce que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a demandé de faire, pour que le monde sache que j’aime le Père.

sw.L: Sitazungumza nanyi mengi zaidi, kwa kuwa mtawala wa ulimwengu yuaja, naye ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hana chochote; \v 31 lakini ili ulimwengu upate kujua kwamba nampenda Baba, na jinsi Baba alivyoniagiza, ndivyo ninavyotenda.
sw.B: Sitasema mengi zaidi nanyi, kwa sababu mtawala wa ulimwengu anakuja. Hana mamlaka yoyote juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \v 31 Lakini ili ulimwengu ujue kwamba nampenda Baba, ninafanya kama vile Baba alivyoniamuru.
sw.R: Sitazungumza nanyi kwa muda mrefu zaidi, kwa sababu Shetani, mtawala wa ulimwengu, anakuja. Hana nguvu yoyote juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \v 31 Lakini ninafanya kile hasa ambacho Baba ameniambia nifanye, ili ulimwengu ujue kwamba nampenda Baba.

vi.L: Ta sẽ không còn nói nhiều với các con nữa, vì kẻ cai trị thế gian đang đến, và nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hắn không có gì cả; \v 31 nhưng để thế gian biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương Cha, và Cha đã truyền lệnh cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thế nào, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm như vậy.
vi.B: Ta sẽ không nói nhiều với các con nữa, vì kẻ cai trị thế gian đang đến. Hắn không có quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 31 Nhưng để thế gian biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương Cha, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm đúng như điều Cha đã truyền cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta sẽ không còn nói chuyện lâu với các con nữa, vì Sa-tan, kẻ cai trị thế gian, đang đến. Hắn không có quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 31 Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm đúng những gì Cha đã bảo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm, để thế gian biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thương Cha.

ko.L: 나는 더 이상 너희와 많은 말을 하지 않을 것이다. 세상의 통치자가 오기 때문이다. 그리고 그는 내 안에 아무것도 가지고 있지 않다. \v 31 다만 세상이 내가 아버지를 사랑한다는 것을 알게 하려고, 아버지께서 내게 명령하신 그대로 내가 행한다.
ko.B: 이제 나는 너희와 더 많은 말을 하지 않겠다. 세상의 통치자가 오고 있기 때문이다. 그는 나를 어떻게 할 아무런 권한도 없다. \v 31 그러나 내가 아버지를 사랑한다는 것을 세상이 알도록, 나는 아버지께서 내게 명령하신 그대로 행한다.
ko.R: 나는 이제 너희와 오래 이야기하지 못할 것이다. 세상의 통치자인 사탄이 오고 있기 때문이다. 그는 나를 어떻게 할 힘이 없다. \v 31 그러나 나는 아버지께서 내게 하라고 하신 일을 그대로 한다. 내가 아버지를 사랑한다는 것을 세상이 알게 하려는 것이다.

pt.L: Já não falarei muitas coisas com vocês, pois vem o governante do mundo; e em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} ele não tem nada; \v 31 mas, para que o mundo saiba que eu amo o Pai, e assim como o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ordenou, assim eu faço.
pt.B: Não vou falar muito mais com vocês, pois o governante do mundo está vindo. Ele não tem domínio algum sobre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. \v 31 Mas, para que o mundo saiba que eu amo o Pai, faço exatamente o que o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ordenou.
pt.R: Não vou conversar com vocês por muito mais tempo, porque Satanás, o governante do mundo, está vindo. Ele não tem poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. \v 31 Mas eu faço exatamente o que o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mandou fazer, para que o mundo saiba que eu amo o Pai.

decisions.choice: the ruler of the world: Satan, now coming against Jesus through those who arrest him
decisions.reason: The same title as in 12:31 and 16:11, there with "this world". He is the devil, who has put the betrayal into Judas's heart and entered him (13:2, 27); his coming is the coming of Judas and the arresting party (18:2-3).

decisions.choice: he has nothing in me: he has no claim on Jesus and no hold over him
alternatives: there is nothing in Jesus that belongs to him
he will find nothing in Jesus to accuse
decisions.reason: The phrase, "in me he has nothing", is a way of saying that the devil has no rights over Jesus and no power to take him. Jesus has no sin that would give him a hold (8:46). So Jesus's death is not the devil's victory: Jesus lays down his life of his own accord (10:18). The other readings come to nearly the same thing.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause goes with "so I do": the SBLGNT puts a full stop after "I do"
alternatives: the purpose clause goes with "Rise, let us go from here": so that the world may know that I love the Father and do as he commanded, rise, let us go
decisions.reason: The Greek has no punctuation of its own. With the SBLGNT, the sentence ends at "I do", and "but so that the world may know" leads to what Jesus does: he obeys the Father, and that obedience shows his love. The "and" before "just as" is then loosely attached, as often in John. The text can also be punctuated with a comma at "I do", so that the purpose clause leads into the command to rise and go out, to meet the ruler who is coming. Both give the same picture: Jesus goes to his death to obey the Father.

decisions.choice: Jesus's love for the Father is shown in his doing what the Father commanded, that is, going to the cross
decisions.reason: This is the only place in the Gospels where Jesus says in so many words that he loves the Father. He shows it as he asks his disciples to show their love: by keeping commands (14:15, 21). The command is that he lay down his life and take it up again (10:18; 12:49-50). The world, set against God, will see this at the cross (12:32; 17:21, 23).

decisions.choice: Satan, the ruler of the world
decisions.reason: As in 12:31, Readable names Satan, whom the title means (meaning decision m1); Jesus is the one speaking, and he knows who the ruler is. Every level keeps the title as in 12:31; here the Greek has "the world" without "this".

decisions.choice: He has no hold on me (B); no power over me (R); Readable puts the purpose clause last
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (meaning decision m2). Readable puts what Jesus does first and the reason after, which is easier to follow; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: el gobernante (L, B); Satanás, el que gobierna (R)
decisions.reason: As at 12:31.

decisions.choice: no tiene ningún poder sobre mí
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: le prince du monde (L, B); Satan, celui qui domine le monde (R)
decisions.reason: "Prince" in its older sense of "ruler" is the usual French title for this figure (12:31; 16:11) and is still understood in this phrase, though today "prince" mostly means a king's son. Readable names Satan, as the English does (meaning decision m1), and says what the title means. A reviewer should check that 12:31 and 16:11 use the same French.

decisions.choice: mtawala wa ulimwengu; Shetani added at Readable
decisions.reason: As at 12:31: "mtawala" (ruler), and Readable names him, as the English does. "Naye" here is the ruler, so it carries no reader setting.

decisions.choice: kẻ cai trị thế gian; hắn
alternatives: người cai trị thế gian; nó
decisions.reason: For Satan, Vietnamese uses the words that mark an enemy: "kẻ" (one who, with a negative tone) and the pronoun "hắn". This differs from Judas in 13:27, who is the neutral "người ấy".

decisions.choice: "세상의 통치자" at every level
decisions.reason: "통치자" is the plain modern word for one who rules; "임금" (king) is the wording of familiar versions and sounds like a monarch. The same term is used wherever John has this title (12:31; 16:11).

decisions.choice: o governante do mundo
decisions.reason: "Príncipe", the traditional word, now means a king's son to most readers; the title means the one who rules (meaning decision m1). "Governante" says that plainly; "chefe" sounds like a boss at work.

records.literal_gloss: Rise, let us go from here.

en.L: Rise, let us go from here.
en.B: Get up; let us go from here.
en.R: Get up. Let us leave this place.

vi.L: Hãy đứng dậy, chúng ta đi khỏi đây.
vi.B: Hãy đứng dậy; chúng ta đi khỏi đây.
vi.R: Đứng dậy nào. Chúng ta hãy rời khỏi chỗ này.

decisions.choice: rise: get up from the table where they have been reclining at the meal
alternatives: rise in the sense of being raised
decisions.reason: At a festive meal people reclined on couches (13:23, 25). The verb means to get up, here from the meal, ready to leave.

decisions.choice: a real call to leave, though the talk goes on and the departure is told only at 18:1
alternatives: they leave now and Jesus goes on speaking on the way
the farewell talks were joined together and this call once led straight to 18:1
the words are a call to go out to meet what is coming, more than a signal to walk out
decisions.reason: The words are plain: Jesus tells them to get up and go. Yet chapters 15 to 17 follow without any mention of moving, and only in 18:1 does John say that Jesus went out with his disciples across the Kidron valley. It may be that they leave now and the talk and prayer of chapters 15 to 17 are spoken on the way. Or the farewell discourses may have been joined together, so that 14:31 once led straight to 18:1. "Let us go" may also be a call to go out and meet the ruler of the world (14:30) in obedience, whenever they moved. The text does not settle which is right.

decisions.choice: Get up; let us go from here (B); Let us leave this place (R)
decisions.reason: "Get up" is the everyday command for rising from a table; "Rise" and "Arise" sound formal. Readable says plainly where they are going: away from the place of the meal.

decisions.choice: Levántense / Levantaos
decisions.reason: Get up from the table (meaning decision m1); the reflexive sits inside the span.

decisions.choice: chúng ta
decisions.reason: "Let us go" includes Jesus and the disciples together, so the inclusive "chúng ta".
